source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a 114 MW, 685,000 square foot data center in Sterling, Virginia, and the third largest of the 25 Virginia facilities that publish capacity.

The published Virginia total is 1,603 MW across 330 mapped data centers, so this single campus is 7.1 percent of the state's disclosed IT load. That concentration is the point. A state with hundreds of mapped facilities has only 25 that disclose a megawatt figure, and one of them carries a fourteenth of the disclosed load. The disclosed total is a floor, not a measure, because most mapped facilities publish nothing.

For AI specifically, 114 MW is the unit that matters. At 400 watts per rack it supports roughly 285 accelerator-dense racks, or about 2,280 high-end GPUs at 8 per rack. That is training and serving capacity at scale, and it sits in Ashburn, inside Northern Virginia's existing power and network backbone. The building is not the constraint here. The power feeding it is.

What the data does not cover is whether that power can grow. Grid constraints on further Virginia expansion are not published, and no interconnection queue, utility, or generation figure appears. LEED certification speaks to how the facility is operated, not to how much additional load the surrounding grid can absorb. The 114 MW is a snapshot of permitted and built capacity, not a forecast of what comes next.
